_readme: Grammar structures in the Telugu course, read by tools/grammar-check.mjs.
One entry per structure. For each one:
introducedIn  the lesson that TEACHES it (vocab teach screen or a grammarNote that explains it).
null = the course uses it but never teaches it.
basis         the curriculum text the tag rests on, so you can check it without opening curriculum.js.
confidence    'sure' = quoted from a grammarNote / vocab gloss; 'guess' = my reading, please confirm.
detect        regexes run over each drill answer (lowercased, punctuation stripped, whole words).
A drill REQUIRES a structure only if its correct answer AND every acceptable form match;
if some accepted form avoids it, the drill merely EXPOSES it.
Empty detect = not auto-detectable, so only (2) 'too many at once' sees it.
except        whole tokens that match detect but are not this structure (lexical items).
Edit freely. The tool re-reads this file on every run; nothing else depends on it.

structures.name: -nu verb ending = 'I'
structures.basis: L1 grammarNote: 'The end of the word tells you who: unnanu is "I am", unnaru is "you are"'. L11 note repeats it.

structures.name: -ru verb ending = polite 'you' / respectful 'he, she'
structures.basis: L1 grammarNote: 'unnaru is "you are". Unnaru also means "he is" or "she is", said with respect.'

structures.name: -vu verb ending = informal 'you'
structures.basis: L1 grammarNote: 'With a close friend, say unnavu.' Mentioned once, never drilled.

structures.name: 'X is Y' with no verb
structures.basis: L2 phrase 'Idhi pusthakam' = 'This is a book' and the note contrasting it with 'ee pusthakam'. Not stated as a rule anywhere.

structures.name: question word after the thing asked about (no word-order change)
structures.example: Idhi emiti? Illu ekkada? Meeru ela unnaru?
structures.basis: L2 grammarNote: 'Question words usually come near the end in Telugu, after the thing you're asking about.' L1 already drills 'Meeru ela unnaru' as a chunk.

structures.name: ee/aa before a noun vs idhi/adhi standing alone
structures.basis: L2 vocab 'Ee = This (before a noun)' and grammarNote contrasting it with idhi.

structures.name: noun changes shape before an ending (illu -> inti-)
structures.basis: L3 grammarNote: 'Here's intiki, "to the house".' It shows the form but never says illu becomes inti-; I'm treating the showing as the introduction.

structures.name: -ki/-ku = 'to' (direction)
structures.basis: L3 grammarNote: 'The -ki goes on the end of the word, never in front.'

structures.name: -andi = polite request ('please ...')
structures.basis: L10 grammarNote: 'The -andi at the end makes it polite.' But L3 already drills 'Akkada vellandi' and 'Intiki vellandi' with no explanation of -andi (L16's note even says '-andi from lesson 3'). Set to 10 because that is where it is EXPLAINED; change to 3 if showing counts.

structures.name: bare verb = informal command
structures.basis: L3 vocab 'Vellu = Go'. The course never says that the bare form is the blunt/informal command, nor contrasts it with -andi until L16.

structures.name: undi = 'it is / there is' (things, places)
structures.basis: L3 vocab 'Undi = It is / there is'.

structures.name: object + kaavali/oddu, no subject ('water is wanted')
structures.basis: L4 grammarNote: 'Two words, no "I". Neeru kaavali means "water is wanted"'.

structures.name: naaku ('to me') as the subject of want/like/have/feel
structures.example: naaku ishtam, naaku gurthundi, naaku pani undi
structures.basis: L5 vocab 'Naaku = To me / I have'. L4's note mentions 'naaku neeru kaavali' first; L20's note calls it 'another "to me" sentence'.

structures.name: naa/mee/ayana before a noun = my/your/his
structures.example: naa peru, mee pusthakam, ayana katha
structures.basis: L5 grammarNote: 'Naa ("my") goes in front of the thing, like ee does.'

structures.name: ayana/ame = respectful he/she (and not idhi for people)
structures.basis: L5 grammarNote: 'Ayana means "he" or "his", said with respect.' L6 note adds that idhi for a person is rude.

structures.name: number before noun; okati -> oka
structures.basis: L7 grammarNote: 'Okati became oka because a thing comes after it.'

structures.name: plural -lu (pusthakam -> pusthakalu)
structures.basis: L8 vocab 'Lu = (Plural suffix)' and grammarNote: 'Pusthakam dropped -am and took -alu.'

structures.name: adjective before the noun
structures.basis: L9 phrases (Pedda illu, Manchi snehithudu). No note states the rule; English has the same order, so arguably not a new structure at all.

structures.name: -tunn- = '-ing' now
structures.basis: L11 vocab (Chestunnanu = I am doing ...). L3's note promises it 'in lesson 11'.

structures.name: past tense (chesanu, vellanu)
structures.basis: L13 vocab (Chesanu = I did ...) and grammarNote on changing -nu for who.

structures.name: future/habitual -t-anu (chestanu, velthanu)
structures.basis: L14 vocab and grammarNote: 'For "I will eat", drop the -unn-: tintanu.'

structures.name: ledu = 'is not / there isn't' after the thing
structures.basis: L15 vocab 'Ledu = No/Not' and grammarNote: 'Ledu also means "is not" or "there isn't".'

structures.name: noun + -ga = state/manner ('happily', 'tired')
structures.basis: L26 grammarNote: 'naaku ... -ga undi, or nenu ... -ga unnanu'. That is the first explanation, but L16, L20, L24 and L25 already drill santhoshamga. Baga/tvaraga/mellaga (L16) are taught as whole words, so excluded.

structures.name: noun + chey- = 'do X' (vanta chey = cook)
structures.basis: L18 phrase 'annam vanta chestunnanu', vocab 'Vanta = Cook'. Nothing explains that vanta is a noun and chey- makes it a verb. 'pani chey' (L11) is literal 'do work', not counted.

structures.name: postpositions after the noun (lo, paina, kindha, tho, daggara)
structures.example: inti lo, naa tho, naa daggara
structures.basis: L21 grammarNote: 'These five words go AFTER the thing, not before.'

structures.name: -galanu 'I can' / -lenu 'I can't'
structures.basis: L22 grammarNote: 'cheya-, then -galanu for "can", or -lenu for "can't".'

structures.name: -aali = must
structures.basis: L23 grammarNote: 'Add -aali to mean "must".'

structures.name: two clauses joined (kani, endukante, mariyu between verbs)
structures.example: Nenu vellali kani naaku pani undi
structures.basis: L24 vocab Kani/Endukante/Leda. L13 conversation already joins two verbs with mariyu ('Nenu vellanu mariyu thinnanu'); I only detect kani/endukante so mariyu-between-nouns (L10) is not counted.

structures.name: -te/-the = 'if'
structures.basis: L25 vocab (Unte = If there is ...). No grammarNote in L25 explains how -te is formed.

structures.name: -aa on the verb = yes/no question
structures.basis: L26 vocab 'Unnara = Are you?'. Taught as one word; the -aa ending is never named, so a learner cannot form any other yes/no question.

structures.name: nundi = 'from' after the place
structures.basis: L30 vocab 'Nundi = From'.
